job.title: Accountant
job.description:
Financial Accountant — CBD | National Multi-Site Business

This is an opportunity to join a well-established national organisation where Finance plays a critical role in supporting operational performance, investment decisions and sustainable growth. You will work in a dynamic, commercially focused environment, partnering with operational and corporate stakeholders to deliver accurate reporting, strong controls and meaningful financial insight.

About the Role Reporting to the Financial Accounting Manager, you will be a key member of the Financial Accounting team. This is a varied, hands-on role with responsibility across month-end reporting, reconciliations, process improvement, and finance automation initiatives.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Prepare and post month-end journals, including accruals, prepayments and other accounting adjustments.
  • Complete high-volume branch bank reconciliations across a national network.
  • Support month-end, quarter-end and year-end financial close activities.
  • Maintain the accuracy, integrity and completeness of the general ledger.
  • Investigate financial variances, resolve issues and provide clear commentary where required.
  • Assist with monthly management reporting, financial analysis and ad hoc reporting requirements.
  • Prepare, maintain and review balance-sheet reconciliations.
  • Monitor outstanding reconciling items and ensure these are cleared in a timely manner.
  • Support fixed-asset accounting, including depreciation and asset-register processes.
  • Maintain strong financial controls, compliance standards and documentation.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to ensure financial data is accurate, complete and reliable.
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual accounting processes and reduce reliance on spreadsheets or repetitive tasks.
  • Contribute to finance transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives.
  • Improve reporting efficiency, workflow quality and data accuracy across the finance function.
About You

You will be a technically capable accountant with a strong foundation in financial accounting, reconciliations and month-end reporting. You are comfortable managing competing priorities, working through complex data and taking ownership of issues through to resolution.
You will also bring a naturally curious mindset—you ask "why," challenge inefficient processes constructively and look for practical ways to improve the finance function.
 
Skills and experience 
  • A degree qualification in Accounting, Commerce or Finance.
  • CA or CPA qualifications or working towards.
  • At least four years' experience in an Accountant or similar financial-accounting role.
  • Experience in a multi-site environment and high transactional environment.
  • Advanced Excel skills and confidence working with large data sets.
  • Experience using ERP systems in a commercially focused environment, SAP Highly regarded.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and financial-control capability.
  • Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across the business.
Why You'll Love This Opportunity
  • Join a recognised national organisation with a strong multi-site footprint
  • Play a visible role in supporting a business during a busy period of growth and transformation.
  • A collaborative team environment with scope to build stakeholder relationships across the business.
  • Hybrid working arrangement — 2 days WFH

  • Manage the operational and financial performance of the department, including P&L, revenue, operating costs, service billing, inventory, travel budgets and business plan delivery.
  • Drive aftermarket growth through spare parts sales, field service activity, maintenance agreements, service inspections, upgrades and equipment modernisation opportunities.

  • Support and develop distributor capability through technical training, product support programs and practical guidance on commissioning, maintenance and repair.
  • Build strong working relationships with customers, distributors, key accounts and internal sales leaders to improve customer outcomes and identify commercial opportunities.
  • Analyse recurring technical and service issues, identify trends and implement practical improvements to reduce future equipment, maintenance and customer support concerns.
  • Champion safety, compliance and best practice service standards, including support for incident investigations and product related safety matters.
  • Provide regular reporting on order intake, billing, warranty, inventory, operational performance, budget variances and business plan objectives.
  • Travel regularly throughout Australia/ New Zealand including regional or remote customer locations.

Key Capabilities:
  • Proven experience leading a Parts and Service, Aftermarket, Product Support, Technical Service or Service Operations function within heavy machinery or capital equipment.
  • Strong technical understanding of mechanical, hydraulic and electrical systems.
  • Experience diagnosing, commissioning, maintaining or repairing cranes, lifting equipment, mobile plant or comparable heavy machinery.
  • Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching, performance management and building capable technical or operational teams.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing budgets, revenue, P&L, inventory and operational performance.
  • A customer focused mindset and the ability to manage complex relationships with distributors, dealers, key accounts and end user customers.
  • The ability to prioritise competing operational demands, solve problems calmly and lead teams through technical or people related challenges.
  • Relevant engineering, mechanical or technical qualifications; an Engineering Degree will be highly regarded.
  • Flexibility and willingness to travel extensively across ANZ, including to regional and remote sites.
